subject: [Follow-up] Marketplace enablement questionnaire & procurement path
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Roy <sasha.roy@datastream.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: [Follow-up] Marketplace enablement questionnaire & procurement path

Hi Sasha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can map the right commercial route and get procurement comfortable:

- Your team expressed preference for AWS Marketplace (SaaS Contract) to keep procurement simple. Confirmed?
- You mentioned a corporate PO process for platform purchases — is that for all purchases or only for >$50k/year?
- Any blockers for a managed SaaS subscription (vs. private deployment) — e.g., data residency, IP restrictions, or SOC2 evidence requests?

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll run through a short marketplace enablement checklist (attached) to flag any gaps.
2) If Marketplace is preferred, we’ll share the estimated listing timeline and a stub SOW for any onboarding services (attached: Datastream-SOW-draft.docx).
3) If PO is required, our finance team will prepare standard invoice/PO flow and a sample contract amendment — to be routed to procurement@datastream.ai.

Can you confirm procurement contact and preferred billing path (Card / PO / AWS Marketplace)? If you can share any procurement policy doc, that’ll help us surface exact ask-to-sign steps.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate on our side once I have that.

Best,
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Attach: Redwood-Marketplace-Checklist-v1.pdf
From: Sasha Roy <sasha.roy@datastream.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datastream.ai
Date: 2027-10-05T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Follow-up] Marketplace enablement questionnaire & procurement path

Thanks Karthik — great summary. Quick answers below and attaching our procurement policy for reference.

- Marketplace: yes, AWS Marketplace is preferred by our Procurement and Legal because it simplifies internal chargebacks.
- PO threshold: any subscription above $25k/yr requires a PO and routing through our AP team.
- Compliance: we’ll need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short data processing agreement addendum; security is a must though we prefer SaaS over private if evidence is available.

Procurement contact is:
Procurement Team <procurement@datastream.ai>
They manage the PO creation and approvals.

Attached: Datastream-Procurement-Policy.pdf

One more ask: can you confirm approximate timing to get an offer live on AWS Marketplace (listing + procurement acceptance)? Our target is Q4 start of pilot.

Thanks,
Sasha Roy
Head of Platform Ops | Datastream Inc
Attach: Datastream-Procurement-Policy.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-05T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Follow-up] Marketplace enablement questionnaire & procurement path

Quick internal note —

Thanks for the heads up Karthik. A couple tactical suggestions before we reply to Procurement: 

- Offer a Marketplace-first path + a backup PO route. If Procurement insists on PO, we can do an initial pilot on card for 30 days to de-risk exec signoff, then convert to PO once they have approvals.
- Confirm whether they need Redwood to be the AWS Marketplace seller or a listing via an AWS SaaS contract aggregation partner — that impacts timeline.
- Ask procurement for a sample PO and approval SLA so Finance can map the invoice flow.

I’ll draft the short marketplace enablement email and attach the checklist. Jordan, can you confirm estimated listing lead time (best-case vs realistic) and any extra items for SOC2 evidence?

—Marissa
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Roy <sasha.roy@datastream.ai>, procurement@datastream.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-06T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & proposed materials for Marketplace pilot (Q4)

Hi Sasha / Procurement team — looping you both in with a proposed path and attached checklist to accelerate approval. Summary: 

1) Marketplace-first (preferred): Redwood will prepare an AWS SaaS listing + standard SaaS contract. Estimated time to publish: 3–4 weeks best-case, 6–8 weeks realistic (depending on listing reviews).
2) PO fallback: If PO is required immediately, we can invoice on a monthly cadence; please share your sample PO template and approvals SLA.
3) Security evidence: attaching SOC2 pack link and our short DPA addendum for procurement review.

Attachments: Redwood-Marketplace-Checklist-v1.pdf, Datastream-SOW-draft.docx
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRDw-example (SOC2 pack)

Action items:
- Sasha / procurement@datastream.ai: confirm preferred path (Marketplace vs PO) and share sample PO if PO path.
- Procurement: confirm internal SLA for PO issuance (days).
- Marissa / Jordan / Karthik: we’ll prep marketplace listing materials on receipt of confirmation and push listing priority internally.

If Marketplace works, we’ll send a stub order form and DocuSign link for signature and then initiate the listing.

Thanks — Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Attach: Redwood-Marketplace-Checklist-v1.pdf, Datastream-SOW-draft.docx
